content: Administer one to two sachets orally once or twice daily. Place the granules on the tongue and swallow them with 250 mL of water. For individuals older than 12 years, the dosage is the same as the adult dose. For children under 12 years, the safety and efficacy of this treatment have not been established. Both sterculia and deflazacort can reduce serum potassium levels. Therefore, caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Sterculia may also reduce the effects of sodium picosulfate through an unspecified interaction mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. Potential side effects include constipation, flatulence, abdominal cramping, and fecal impaction. Rare but serious adverse effects may include hypersensitivity reactions, gastrointestinal obstruction, fecal impaction, symptoms resembling appendicitis or an acute surgical abdomen, gastrointestinal ulceration, dysphagia, and rectal bleeding. It is essential to consume adequate amounts of water with this preparation to minimize the risk of these complications. This treatment is not recommended in cases of abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or fever. Additionally, it is advised to separate the administration of this preparation from other medications by at least two hours, as laxatives may interfere with the absorption of other drugs. Regarding pregnancy, there is no specific category assigned. However, the preparation is generally considered acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. For lactation, there is no available data, but since the preparation is not absorbed systemically, it is unlikely to pose a risk to breastfeeding infants.
